questions.korean: 그때 그 결정을 내리지 않았다면, 지금 여기 없을 거야.
answers: Had I not made that decision back then, I wouldn't be here now.
If I hadn't made that decision, I wouldn't be where I am today.
questions.hint: Had I not + p.p. (도치 가정법)
questions.explanation: Had I not = If I had not (도치)

questions.korean: 그게 사실이라면 모든 게 달라졌을 텐데.
answers: Were that true, everything would have been different.
If that were true, everything would have changed.
questions.hint: Were + 주어 + 형용사 (도치 가정법 과거)
questions.explanation: Were that true = If that were true (도치)

questions.korean: 내가 그의 입장이었다면 똑같이 했을 거야.
answers: Had I been in his position, I would have done the same.
If I had been in his shoes, I'd have acted the same way.
questions.hint: Had I been in his position/shoes
questions.explanation: in his shoes = 그의 입장에서

questions.korean: 조금만 더 일찍 출발했더라면 기차를 탈 수 있었을 텐데.
answers: Had we left a little earlier, we could have caught the train.
If only we had set off a bit sooner, we would have made the train.
questions.hint: Had we left earlier, could have caught
questions.explanation: set off = 출발하다

questions.korean: 그런 도움이 없었더라면 절대 해내지 못했을 거야.
answers: Without that help, I could never have pulled it off.
But for that support, I would never have succeeded.
questions.hint: Without ~ / But for ~ = ~가 없었더라면
questions.explanation: pull it off = 해내다, but for = without

questions.korean: 그제서야 나는 실수를 깨달았어.
answers: Only then did I realize my mistake.
It was only then that I became aware of my error.
questions.hint: Only then + 조동사 + 주어 (도치)
questions.explanation: Only then = 그제서야 (부정어 도치)

questions.korean: 결코 그런 말을 한 적이 없어.
answers: Never have I said such a thing.
At no point did I say that.
questions.hint: Never + have + 주어 + p.p. (부정어 도치)
questions.explanation: 부정어(Never, Rarely, Seldom) + 도치

questions.korean: 그가 들어온 순간 모두가 조용해졌어.
answers: No sooner had he entered than everyone fell silent.
The moment he walked in, everyone went quiet.
questions.hint: No sooner had + 주어 + p.p. + than
questions.explanation: No sooner ~ than = ~하자마자

questions.korean: 그 영화가 얼마나 훌륭한지!
answers: What a wonderful movie it is!
How amazing the movie is!
questions.hint: What a + 형용사 + 명사! / How + 형용사!
questions.explanation: What = 명사 강조, How = 형용사/부사 강조

questions.korean: 좀처럼 이런 기회는 오지 않아.
answers: Seldom does such an opportunity arise.
Rarely do we get a chance like this.
questions.hint: Seldom/Rarely + 조동사 + 주어 (도치)

questions.korean: 날씨를 고려하면, 우리는 여행을 취소해야 했어.
answers: Given the weather, we had to cancel the trip.
Taking the weather into account, we had no choice but to cancel.
questions.hint: Given ~ / Taking ~ into account = ~를 고려하면
questions.explanation: take into account = 고려하다

questions.korean: 그 프로젝트를 마무리하면서 우리는 많은 것을 배웠어.
answers: Having completed the project, we learned a great deal.
Finishing the project, we gained valuable experience.
questions.hint: Having + p.p. = 먼저 완료 후 → 분사구문

questions.korean: 솔직히 말하자면, 그 결정은 최선이 아니었어.
answers: Frankly speaking, that was not the best decision.
To put it bluntly, it wasn't the right call.
questions.hint: Frankly speaking / To put it bluntly = 솔직히 말하자면
questions.explanation: to put it bluntly = 직설적으로 말하자면

questions.korean: 두 팔을 벌리고, 그는 군중을 환영했어.
answers: With his arms wide open, he welcomed the crowd.
Arms outstretched, he embraced the crowd.
questions.hint: with + 명사 + 형용사/p.p. (부대상황)

questions.korean: 일이 뜻대로 풀리지 않으면서, 그는 포기할 뻔했어.
answers: With things not going as planned, he almost gave up.
Things not going his way, he was on the verge of giving up.
questions.hint: With things not going + as planned
questions.explanation: on the verge of = ~하기 직전에

questions.korean: 그가 했던 것은 모두가 그를 놀라게 했어.
answers: What he did surprised everyone.
Everything he did left everyone astonished.
questions.hint: What he did = 그가 한 것 (선행사 포함 관계대명사)

questions.korean: 어떤 선택을 하든, 결과를 받아들여야 해.
answers: Whatever choice you make, you have to accept the consequences.
Whichever path you choose, you must be prepared for the outcome.
questions.hint: Whatever / Whichever + 명사 + 주어 + 동사

questions.korean: 그가 어디를 가든 그를 따라다녔어.
answers: Wherever he went, they followed him.
He was followed wherever he went.
questions.hint: wherever = 어디를 ~하든

questions.korean: 그녀가 아무리 열심히 해도 충분하지 않은 것 같았어.
answers: However hard she tried, it never seemed to be enough.
No matter how hard she worked, it felt like it was never sufficient.
questions.hint: However + 형용사/부사 + 주어 + 동사 = 아무리 ~해도

questions.korean: 그 이유가 무엇이든, 그는 사과를 해야 해.
answers: Whatever the reason may be, he owes an apology.
Regardless of the reason, an apology is in order.
questions.hint: Whatever the reason may be = 이유가 무엇이든
questions.explanation: an apology is in order = 사과가 마땅하다

questions.korean: 그것은 결코 쉽지 않은 결정이었어.
answers: It was anything but an easy decision.
It was far from an easy choice.
questions.hint: anything but = far from = 결코 ~가 아닌
questions.explanation: anything but = 전혀 ~이 아닌

questions.korean: 그건 내가 기대한 것과는 전혀 달라.
answers: That's nothing like what I expected.
That's a far cry from what I had in mind.
questions.hint: nothing like / a far cry from = 전혀 다른
questions.explanation: a far cry from = 큰 차이가 있는

questions.korean: 그 책은 읽을 가치가 있어.
answers: The book is worth reading.
It's a book worth your time.
questions.hint: be worth + ~ing = ~할 가치가 있다

questions.korean: 나는 더 이상 참을 수가 없어.
answers: I can no longer put up with it.
I've had it up to here.
questions.hint: no longer = 더 이상 ~않다, put up with = 참다
questions.explanation: I've had it up to here = 더 이상 못 참겠다 (구어체)

questions.korean: 그 문제는 생각보다 훨씬 복잡해.
answers: The problem is far more complex than I thought.
The issue is a lot more complicated than it seems.
questions.hint: far/a lot more + 형용사 + than I thought

questions.korean: 이 에세이는 기후 변화의 영향을 살펴볼 것이다.
answers: This essay will examine the effects of climate change.
This paper aims to explore the impact of climate change.
questions.hint: examine / explore = 살펴보다, 탐구하다

questions.korean: 이 주장을 뒷받침하는 증거가 있다.
answers: There is evidence to support this argument.
The following evidence supports this claim.
questions.hint: evidence to support / supports this claim

questions.korean: 반대 의견에도 불구하고, 그 이론은 여전히 유효하다.
answers: Despite opposing views, the theory remains valid.
Notwithstanding the counterarguments, the theory holds.
questions.hint: despite / notwithstanding = ~에도 불구하고
questions.explanation: notwithstanding = 격식체의 despite

questions.korean: 이 연구의 한계점 중 하나는 표본 크기가 작다는 것이다.
answers: One limitation of this study is the small sample size.
A key constraint of this research is its limited sample size.
questions.hint: one limitation / key constraint of this study is ~
questions.explanation: constraint = limitation (제약, 한계)

questions.korean: 향후 연구에서 이 주제를 더 깊이 탐구해야 한다.
answers: Future research should explore this topic more deeply.
Further investigation is needed to fully understand this subject.
questions.hint: future research / further investigation = 향후 연구

topic: 뉘앙스 - used to / would / be used to

questions.korean: 나는 어렸을 때 매일 피아노를 치곤 했어.
answers: I used to play the piano every day when I was young.
I would play the piano every day as a child.
questions.hint: used to + 동사원형 = 과거 습관 (지금은 아님)
questions.explanation: used to = 과거 상태/습관, would = 과거 반복 행동

questions.korean: 나는 혼자 여행하는 것에 익숙해.
answers: I'm used to traveling alone.
I'm accustomed to traveling by myself.
questions.hint: be used to + ~ing = ~에 익숙하다
questions.explanation: used to (동사) ≠ be used to (형용사+전치사)

questions.korean: 나는 매운 음식을 먹는 것에 익숙해지고 있어.
answers: I'm getting used to eating spicy food.
I'm becoming accustomed to spicy food.
questions.hint: get used to + ~ing = 익숙해져 가고 있다

questions.korean: 우리는 예전에 이 동네에 살곤 했어.
answers: We used to live in this neighborhood.
We used to call this neighborhood home.
questions.hint: used to live = 과거에 살았다 (지금은 아님)

questions.korean: 처음엔 그 소음이 귀찮았지만, 이제는 익숙해.
answers: At first, the noise bothered me, but now I'm used to it.
The noise used to bother me, but I've gotten used to it.
questions.hint: used to bother / now I'm used to it

questions.korean: 그 결정은 다소 논란의 여지가 있어.
answers: The decision is somewhat controversial.
That decision is a bit contentious, to say the least.
questions.hint: somewhat controversial / a bit contentious = 다소 논란적
questions.explanation: to say the least = 최소한으로 말하더라도

questions.korean: 그것이 항상 최선의 전략이라고 할 수는 없어.
answers: It's not always the most optimal strategy.
One might argue it's not necessarily the best approach.
questions.hint: not always / not necessarily = 항상/반드시 ~이지는 않다

questions.korean: 조심스럽게 표현하자면, 그 발표는 썩 좋지 않았어.
answers: To put it diplomatically, the presentation wasn't great.
If I'm being gentle about it, the presentation left something to be desired.
questions.hint: to put it diplomatically = 외교적으로 말하자면
questions.explanation: leave something to be desired = 아쉬운 점이 있다

questions.korean: 그건 최선의 표현 방식이 아닐 수 있어.
answers: That may not be the most ideal way to put it.
It might not be the best choice of words.
questions.hint: may not be the most ideal / best choice of words

questions.korean: 그의 행동은 다소 적절하지 않다고 볼 수 있어.
answers: His behavior could be considered somewhat inappropriate.
One could argue his conduct was less than appropriate.
questions.hint: could be considered / one could argue = 볼 수 있다, 주장할 수 있다

questions.korean: 그가 도착했을 때, 나는 이미 두 시간 동안 기다리고 있었어.
answers: When he arrived, I had already been waiting for two hours.
By the time he showed up, I had been there for two hours.
questions.hint: had been + ~ing = 과거완료 진행 (과거 특정 시점 이전부터 계속)

questions.korean: 그 영화가 시작할 때쯤에 우리는 이미 도착해 있을 거야.
answers: By the time the movie starts, we will have already arrived.
We'll have gotten there before the movie begins.
questions.hint: By the time + 현재, will have + p.p. (미래완료)
questions.explanation: 미래완료: 미래 특정 시점 이전에 완료될 일

questions.korean: 그는 10년 동안 그 회사를 이끌어왔어.
answers: He has been leading the company for ten years.
He has led the company for a decade.
questions.hint: has been leading (현재완료 진행) / has led (현재완료)

questions.korean: 그들이 발표를 끝냈을 때쯤 나는 이미 그 내용을 알고 있었어.
answers: By the time they finished the announcement, I already knew the content.
When they were done presenting, I had already found out.
questions.hint: by the time + 과거, had already + p.p.

questions.korean: 다음 달이면 우리는 10년째 함께 일한 게 돼.
answers: By next month, we will have been working together for ten years.
Next month marks ten years since we started working together.
questions.hint: By next month, will have been + ~ing (미래완료 진행)

questions.korean: 그는 항상 장단에 맞춰.
answers: He always goes with the flow.
He tends to follow the crowd.
questions.hint: go with the flow = 흐름을 따르다, 장단에 맞추다
questions.explanation: follow the crowd = 대세를 따르다

questions.korean: 그건 아직 공중에 떠 있어. (미결 상태)
answers: That's still up in the air.
It's still undecided.
questions.hint: up in the air = 미결 상태, 불확실한

questions.korean: 그녀는 내 마음을 꿰뚫어 봤어.
answers: She saw right through me.
She could read me like a book.
questions.hint: see right through = 꿰뚫어 보다
questions.explanation: read someone like a book = 완전히 파악하다

questions.korean: 이 프로젝트는 생각보다 훨씬 복잡한 작업이야.
answers: This project is a much bigger undertaking than expected.
This turned out to be a far more complex task than anticipated.
questions.hint: a bigger undertaking / far more complex than expected
questions.explanation: undertaking = 사업, 작업

questions.korean: 나는 그 일에서 손을 뗐어.
answers: I washed my hands of it.
I stepped away from the whole thing.
questions.hint: wash one's hands of = ~에서 손을 떼다
